title: General Brains, Domain-Adapted Worlds
userCorrection: Simulations and digital twins can be improved with world models; they should not be presented as a separate learned-world-model category.
researchAndEditorialReview: Completed by a separate agent at the author’s request and reviewed by the Site owner agent.
editorialNotes: Read and extracted all six uploaded PDF pages; the manuscript's seven main sections, central thesis and substantive research examples are retained.

Corrected the central taxonomy: simulators and digital twins are frameworks/representations that can incorporate and benefit from learned world models; they are not presented as mutually exclusive kinds of learned world model.
Added concrete simulator/twin augmentation with ReDRAW residual latent dynamics and Cosmos visual synthetic-data generation, separating dynamic fidelity from visual richness.

Distinguished domain, task and site specificity, prediction-model adaptation from policy adaptation, action-free V-JEPA 2 from action-conditioned V-JEPA 2-AC, and supervisory LLM reasoning from robot execution/control.

Qualified 'one per site' as the author's architectural bet; it can be a shared base plus adapter or dynamics calibration. V-JEPA 2-AC's zero-shot transfer in two labs and TD-MPC2's multitask transfer do not support claiming dynamics never transfer.

Removed 'Fable', the asserted language-model duopoly and universal claims that self-hosting/small models are obsolete. Kept the author's personal preference for strong shared general reasoning and local predictive infrastructure.
Removed unsupported '75% of the economy' and secondary-source software-GDP percentages rather than publishing them as facts.
Kept the historical METR seven-month finding while specifying its 50%-success benchmark time horizon and human task-time calibration.

Removed a universal few-hours/minutes data promise. Retained exact <62-hour DROID evidence with its limited robot demonstration scope; SimDist and ReDRAW are described according to their reported tested capabilities.

Removed blanket claims that generative world models cannot be adapted and that all latent world models skip rendering entirely. Planning/policy learning in latent space is the relevant distinction; Dreamer can train with reconstruction objectives.
Retained edge latency as the architectural argument, but clarified that the roughly 300M V-JEPA 2-AC predictor is not the entire model and that control-loop performance depends on the full system.
Changed policy training in world models from an asserted 'safe place' to pre-real-trial training/evaluation; prediction and offline evaluation do not establish physical safety.
Clarified progress scoring requires goals/rewards/values; a world model does not inherently know task success.

Verified Atlas, Genie 3, Dreamer 4, the 2026 survey, WorldEvolver, GigaWorld-1, SimDist, ReDRAW and RepWAM against primary or creator sources. WorldEvolver/web-agent evidence is explicitly distinguished from physical-robot evidence.

Added NIST and NVIDIA primary sources for simulation/twin roles. Original Axios GDP and IEEE overview references were not needed after the clarified primary-source treatment; reference numbering was regenerated.
The source manuscript publication date is 2026-10-05. The output deliberately leaves publication date placement to the Site template.

sources.title: Siriwardhana et al. (2023). Improving the Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Models for Open Domain Question Answering. TACL.
sources.supportedClaim: The author's RAG-end2end work adapts retrieval and generation jointly to domain-specific knowledge bases.

sources.title: Brown et al. (2020). Language Models are Few-Shot Learners.
sources.supportedClaim: Scaling autoregressive language models improves task-agnostic few-shot performance; GPT-3 is an example.

sources.title: OpenAI (2023). GPT-4 Technical Report.
sources.supportedClaim: GPT-4 is a large-scale multimodal model with broad language and reasoning capabilities, with documented limitations.

sources.title: Ha and Schmidhuber (2018). World Models.
sources.supportedClaim: Learned compressed temporal representations can support policies trained inside imagined environments.

sources.title: Hafner et al. (2025). Mastering diverse control tasks through world models. Nature.
sources.supportedClaim: Dreamer 3 learns behaviors through latent imagination and is evaluated on over 150 tasks with one algorithm configuration, not one universally deployed site model.

sources.title: Google DeepMind (2025). Genie 3: A new frontier for world models.
sources.supportedClaim: Genie 3 generates interactive environments in real time; this is distinct from verified dynamics or guaranteed robot control.

sources.title: Hafner, Yan and Lillicrap (2025). Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models (Dreamer 4).
sources.supportedClaim: Dreamer 4 learns behaviors in a learned world model from offline Minecraft data, with much of its knowledge extracted from unlabeled video.

sources.title: World Labs (2026). Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence.
sources.supportedClaim: Atlas is presented by its creators as supporting generation, reconstruction and space-time simulation; real site imagery can condition reconstruction.

sources.title: METR (2025). Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks.
sources.supportedClaim: The study's historical roughly seven-month doubling applies to a 50%-success task time horizon on measured software/reasoning tasks, with time calibrated against human experts.

sources.title: Belcak et al. (2025). Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI.
sources.supportedClaim: This position paper argues for small language models in many repeated agent invocations and heterogeneous systems, rather than the end of small models.

sources.title: Hansen, Su and Wang (2024). TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control.
sources.supportedClaim: TD-MPC2 performs planning with a learned implicit, decoder-free latent world model and demonstrates cross-domain multitask capabilities.

sources.title: Assran et al. (2025). V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning.
sources.supportedClaim: Action-free video pretraining is distinct from V-JEPA 2-AC, which learns an approximately 300M action-conditioned predictor on a frozen encoder from under 62 hours of DROID robot trajectories; new-lab robot planning is zero-shot, with no target-site training.

sources.title: Taylor et al. (2023). Enhancing Digital Twins with Advances in Simulation and Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges. Winter Simulation Conference / NIST.
sources.supportedClaim: Simulation investigates physical systems; a digital twin connects a representation/simulation to a physical counterpart, and combining simulation with AI offers additional opportunities.

sources.title: NVIDIA (2025). NVIDIA Launches Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform to Accelerate Physical AI Development.
sources.supportedClaim: Cosmos world foundation models can generate photorealistic videos from controlled Omniverse 3D scenarios to augment training/evaluation data; physics fidelity is not thereby guaranteed.

sources.title: Hou et al. (2026). World Model for Robot Learning: A Comprehensive Survey.
sources.supportedClaim: The survey describes world models supporting policy learning, planning, simulation, evaluation and data generation; it does not establish that the article's three application roles are an exhaustive taxonomy.

sources.title: Gu et al. (2025). Is Your LLM Secretly a World Model of the Internet? Model-Based Planning for Web Agents.
sources.supportedClaim: WebDreamer predicts candidate web-action outcomes before execution; the analogy to physical planning is an inference, not robot evidence.

sources.title: Zhang et al. (2026). Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning (WorldEvolver).
sources.supportedClaim: WorldEvolver revises deployment-time memory/context and filters low-confidence foresight with frozen model parameters; the experiments are in ALFWorld/ScienceWorld, not physical robot control.

sources.title: GigaWorld Team et al. (2026). GigaWorld-1: A Roadmap to Build World Models for Robot Policy Evaluation.
sources.supportedClaim: World-model policy evaluation requires action-faithful, consistent rollouts over long horizons, beyond visual realism; this is not a proof of real-world safety.

sources.title: NVIDIA et al. (2025). Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI.
sources.supportedClaim: Cosmos provides pretrained world foundation models and examples of application-specific post-training.

sources.title: Levy et al. (2026). Simulation Distillation: Pretraining World Models in Simulation for Rapid Real-World Adaptation (SimDist).
sources.supportedClaim: SimDist pretrains from physics simulation and adapts only latent dynamics while transferring the encoder, reward model and value function; demonstrated tasks include manipulation and quadruped locomotion.

sources.title: Lanier et al. (2026; preprint 2025). Adapting World Models with Latent-State Dynamics Residuals (ReDRAW). L4DC / PMLR.
sources.supportedClaim: ReDRAW corrects a simulation-pretrained latent world model with residual dynamics learned from scarce target data; tests include simulated control and physical robot lane following.

sources.title: Wang et al. (2026). RepWAM: World Action Modeling with Representation Visual-Action Tokenizers.
sources.supportedClaim: RepWAM reports advantages from semantic visual-action tokenization in its evaluated manipulation settings, rather than a universal theorem that semantic representations are always best.
